goblins.supervivencia: Don't let them surround you. One goblin is a coward, ten are a firing squad. Look up; they love dropping from the ceiling.
goblins.habilidad: They move through the shadows and use their numbers to overwhelm their prey. If they feel disadvantaged, they will flee to seek reinforcements.
goblins.lore: Hordes of wretched and cunning creatures born in the dark scum of the underground world. Although individually feeble and prone to running, goblins hunt by attacking treacherously like malicious hives. Forging weapons that transmit muddy diseases and cowardly ambushing with primitive bows in alleys, they become dangerous predatory parasites for unwary soldiers.

variantes.supervivencia: Don't use arrows; They will pass between your ribs. Use a heavy mallet or shield to splinter its bones. Remember that they do not feel pain or fear; They will continue attacking until their skulls are dust.
variantes.habilidad: Immune to poison and exhaustion. He cannot be scared or paralyzed. Your bones partially deflect piercing damage.
variantes.lore: The basic skeleton is the simplest result of necromancy: bones reanimated by necrotic magic that obey without question. They lack free will, memory, and purpose beyond the commands of their creator. Although easy for an experienced adventurer to destroy, in large groups they can overwhelm even the most prepared.

variantes.supervivencia: Use full coverage immediately; Its bow has a range of 18 meters and does not stop. Close your distance: in melee they are as fragile as any skeleton.
variantes.habilidad: Specialized in ranged combat with a short bow. Its high Dexterity makes it more accurate than the standard skeleton. In melee he is equally fragile.
variantes.lore: The most cunning necromancers reserve their bow-wielding warriors as skeletal archers, a variant designed to shower intruders with projectiles from elevated positions. Unlike their melee cousins, these do not charge; They wait silently on parapets and towers until something alive crosses their field of vision.

variantes.habitat: Cursed Battlefields, Desecrated Stables, Plains of Death
variantes.supervivencia: Aim at the rider, not the horse. If the rider falls, the horse is left without clear direction. Its speed of 18 meters makes it very difficult to reach on foot: don't run, use spells.
variantes.habilidad: Functions as a mount for undead creatures or necromancers. You don't need to eat, sleep or rest. Charge at full speed with no penalty for scaled terrain.
variantes.lore: Warhorses fallen in battle are easy prey for necromancers seeking mobility in their armies. The skeleton horse does not neigh or breathe; gallops in absolute silence even in the deepest darkness. Many undead generals ride these beasts as a status symbol: their speed is terrifying and they cannot be intimidated.

variantes.habitat: Towers of Fallen Wizards, Tombs of Arcanists
variantes.supervivencia: It is the priority objective: its spells can paralyze or drain life. Close distance to interrupt spells. Radiant damage breaches his magical remains.
variantes.habilidad: He retains the magical memory of his previous life. It can cast Frost Beam, Fire Sphere, and Life Drain. Your concentration is vulnerable if you take physical damage.
variantes.lore: When an arcanist dies without completing his work, sometimes the knowledge remains trapped in the bones themselves. The mage skeleton is not always created; sometimes it emerges alone, guided by the echo of incantations it once mastered. It is more dangerous than the common skeleton precisely because it acts with something resembling intelligence, even if it is only the hollow reflection of what it once was.

variantes.habitat: Abandoned Labyrinths, Deep Dungeons, Underworld Ruins
variantes.supervivencia: Its attack is devastating in open spaces. In narrow corridors it loses effectiveness. Interpose obstacles; It cannot brake easily after a full charge.
variantes.habilidad: If you move at least 10 feet in a straight line toward a target and hit it, the target must exceed Strength DC 14 or be Knocked Down and take an additional 2d8 trampling damage.
variantes.lore: The labyrinths of the ancient world were guarded by living minotaurs. Now, many of those same labyrinths are inhabited by their reanimated remains: colossal skeletons that continue to patrol the same corridors they walked in life. Without the original rage, they do not pursue obsessively, but their brute force is still devastating.

variantes.habitat: Desecrated Temples, Tombs of Serpent Priests, Ancient Crypts
variantes.supervivencia: She is a caster and a fighter at the same time. Prioritizes interrupting their concentration with physical damage. Its bite poisons; have antidotes ready. Radiant damage is your best tool against her.
variantes.habilidad: Retains the arcane or divine abilities of the original naga. Its bite injects paralyzing venom (CON DC 13). Can cast area control and enchantment spells.
variantes.lore: The Skeleton Naga is born when a powerful necromancer captures the spirit of a naga and forces it back into its own remains. The result is a bone snake that retains the intelligence and magic of the original creature, but without pride or will of its own. They are perfect guardians of temples: immune to fatigue, poison and fear, always vigilant, always lethal.

variantes.habitat: Desecrated Dragon Lairs, Cursed Mountain Peaks, Ancient Necropolises
variantes.supervivencia: It is one of the most dangerous creatures a necromancer can create. Its bite drains maximum hit points permanently until the long rest. A single Multiattack (bite + 2 claws + tail) can destroy an entire group. Bludgeoning is the only real vulnerability: use maces, warhammers, or impact spells. Avoid melee unless you have the advantage.
variantes.habilidad: Its bite reduces the target's maximum HP by as much as the damage dealt (until the next long rest), and the Dragon regains those same HP. His Limited Telepathy allows him to transmit images and emotions up to 36 meters, without receiving a response. He retains the intelligence of his previous life although he can no longer speak.
variantes.lore: When a necromancer obtains the remains of a dragon and possesses enough power to revive it, the result is one of the most terrifying works of dark magic. The skeleton dragon retains the personality and intelligence of the creature it once was, trapped in bone and necrotic magic without the ability to express itself. He can no longer exhale his destructive breath or speak, but his bite drains the vitality of the living, his gargantuan mass crushes armies, and his presence radiates a dark melancholy that his enemies perceive as formless terror. To the necromancers who command them, they are the ultimate symbol of what can be achieved without scruples.

fenix.supervivencia: Avoid clumping together, its fiery aura will burn multiple targets. Explodes upon death, so keep your distance when its health is low.
fenix.habilidad: When it drops to 0 hit points, it explodes in a sphere of fire and leaves behind a pile of ashes from which it will be reborn in 1d4 days.
fenix.lore: A majestic bird composed of pure elemental fire. It is said that seeing a phoenix is an omen of both destruction and renewal.

kipine.supervivencia: Do not fight near cliffs; His favorite tactic is to throw you into the void. If you hear its scream, cover your ears or you could be stunned and at the mercy of its claws. Attack him from the solid ground.
kipine.habilidad: A sonic scream capable of deafening and disorienting any adventurer who approaches its nest.
kipine.lore: An aberration born of ancient magic and forgotten experiments of the Blood Wizards. The Kipine combines the ferocity of a terrestrial predator with the agility of the skies. It is said that its claws can pierce steel and that its scream is capable of deafening the brave.

orcos.supervivencia: Don't let them touch you; His physical strength is overwhelming. Attack them from the flanks and use magic to weaken their will before engaging in combat.
orcos.habilidad: When an orc is reduced to 0 HP for the first time, it can make one move and one additional attack before falling, fueled by the rage of its tutelary god Gruumsh. This frenzied fury makes them especially dangerous in the final moments of combat, and many adventurers have died believing they had won. Furthermore, their resistance to pain allows them to continue fighting with injuries that would kill a human instantly.
orcos.lore: Orcs are children of war, shaped by their tutelary god Gruumsh the Destroyer since the dawn of time. Organized into brutal tribes with hierarchies defined by strength and bloodshed, their culture has no room for weakness or compassion. Every orc lives to die in glory on a battlefield; Growing old is considered the greatest shame possible. Their settlements are war camps in perpetual motion, and their leaders, the Warchiefs, accumulate power by conquering other tribes until they form hordes capable of devastating entire villages. However, some travelers have documented exiled orcs who, away from tribes, develop surprising tactical intelligence and even forge pragmatic alliances with other races, suggesting that orc brutality is more cultural than innate.

hobgoblins.supervivencia: Do not attack them from the front if they are in formation. Hobgoblins gain defensive advantage when alongside their allies. Use area magic to break their ranks before engaging in melee combat.
hobgoblins.habilidad: Military discipline and fierce tactics. Hobgoblins are the elite warriors of the goblins and can deal extra damage if an ally is close to the target.
hobgoblins.lore: Military discipline and fierce tactics. Hobgoblins are the warrior elite of the goblins. The chronicles of the Iron Legions mention that they do not flee the battlefield.

kobolds.supervivencia: Don't underestimate them because of their size. If you see one, there are ten more in the shadows. They are masters of tricks; Watch carefully where you step before entering their territory.
kobolds.habilidad: The Kobold has guaranteed advantage on all physical and ranged attack rolls against any enemy if at least one of the Kobold's allies is threatening that prey within 5 feet.
kobolds.lore: Miserable scaly beings purged from the deep subterranean strata, who take blind pride in claiming that their poisonous veins pulse with the majestic blood of chromatic dragons. Cowardly and physically decrepit by nature, a Kobold will rarely take part in a fair and square confrontation. To overcome their pathetic strength, they employ their sadistic hive instincts by turning any musty cave into a deadly labyrinth choked with sharp traps, invisible pits of acid, and narrow passageways infested with scorpions. They love to beg for devotion and slavishly serve under the clutches of ancient wyrms or dark subterranean wizards.

cultistas.supervivencia: Don't try to reason with them; His faith is blind. Attack them by surprise before they can complete their dark rituals. Their robes hide more than just secrets.
cultistas.habilidad: Individuals devoted to a dark faith, often sacrificing their own life for their lord to influence others by allowing one creature to be sacrificed to regenerate another.
cultistas.lore: Individuals devoted to a dark faith, often sacrificing their own lives for their lord. The Shadow Chronicles recount their secret deeds.

lobos.supervivencia: Don't let them surround you. Wolves often attack in packs and use simple tactics to distract their prey. If you see just one, there are probably five more in the shadows.
lobos.habilidad: The alpha wolf emits a chilling howl that summons scattered pack members over a wide radius, attracting 1d4 additional wolves in 1d4 rounds. Their coordinated attacks always aim to knock down the target: if the bite connects, the target must pass a strength test or fall to the ground, leaving themselves vulnerable to attacks from all the other members of the pack around them.
lobos.lore: Wolves are much more than just beasts: they are social predators with tactical intelligence that rivals that of many humanoids. A pack has clear hierarchy, complex body language, and long-term memory of territories and enemies. They know the merchant routes, patrol schedules, and camp blind spots. In the folklore of border towns, the lone wolf crossing the road at night is always an omen: not of his presence, but of that of his entire pack hidden in the trees. Revered as manifestations of the god of the hunt in barbarian cultures, and feared as relentless predators in civilized areas, wolves occupy a dual place in the world's imagination: a symbol of wild freedom and silent death that comes without warning.

osos.supervivencia: If the bear rears up on its hind legs, don't try to dodge backwards; runs to the flanks. His embrace is lethal, but his turning radius is clumsy.
osos.habilidad: His brute strength is enough to shatter armor and bones with ease. They are not just beasts, their survival instinct makes them fearsome adversaries.
osos.lore: Powerful predators of deep forests and high mountain ranges. His brute strength is so overwhelming that it can shatter thick armor and break forged shields with unwanted ease. Revered by wild tribes and feared by woodsmen, they rarely attack unless defending their young; If the forest roared in indignation against whoever hurt it, it would do so with the indomitable paws of the bear.

arana_gigante.supervivencia: Don't let him shoot his nets at you. If the spider envelops you, you will be at its mercy. Use a torch to burn away the cobwebs around it.
arana_gigante.habilidad_titulo: Web Sense, Entangle, and Wall Walker
arana_gigante.habilidad: While you are touching a web, you know the exact location of any creature in contact with it and can pass through it without penalties. Uses his ranged attack Web (Range 9/18 m) to bind and Strongly Immobilize a creature. Its venomous bite finishes off the prey by painfully paralyzing it if it manages to unleash serious damage or knock it down. It can climb and stay on ceilings without needing to make rolls.
arana_gigante.lore: These silk thread monsters are not simple corpulent beasts, but tactical predators who have macabrely honed the art of the ambush. They trace kilometers of translucent fibers between the trunks of leafy forests or shadowy underground cavities. They do not pursue to kill; They merely lurk waiting from the tops. When a victim struggles intertwined, the spider emerges terrifyingly quickly wielding lethal fangs brimming with paralyzing toxin, thus keeping the adventurers alive but prostrate wrapped in thick white cocoons.

variantes.supervivencia: Don't let them get close; Your only weapon is number and persistence. A mortally wounded zombie can still get up once: make sure nothing is left standing.
variantes.habilidad: When he drops to 0 HP, he can make a CON roll (DC 5 + damage taken). If you pass it, you remain at 1 HP instead of dying. Only fails with radiant damage or cutting off the head.
variantes.lore: Corpses reanimated by the simplest of necrotic rituals. They don't think, they don't feel, they don't get tired. They only move forward. The chronicles of the Bone Plagues relate that zombies are always the omen: where there is one, there are hundreds. Destroy the necromancer or the horde has no end.

variantes.habitat: Corrupted Forests, Necrotic Wastes, Defiled Lairs
variantes.resistente: Poison (Immune), Necrotic (Immune), Piercing and Cutting non-magical weapons
variantes.supervivencia: Don't underestimate him for being an animal: his Charge can knock you down in one hit and immediately combines with his claws. Keep your distance and use radiant damage; It's the only thing stopping his Undead Fortress from saving him. Every bite he receives heals him, so prioritize bludgeoning and radiant hits over conventional physical damage.
variantes.habilidad: If he falls to 0 HP, he makes a CON roll (DC 5 + damage taken) to be at 1 HP instead. Each time its bite connects, it regains 1d6 HP. If it moves at least 6 meters in a straight line and strikes with its claws, the target must exceed STR DC 15 or be Knocked Down.
variantes.lore: A colossal bear carcass covered in rotting flesh and exposed bones, advancing with heavy steps and insatiable hunger. His eyes shine with a strange light that does not belong to any living being. These spawns are the result of dark necrotic rituals or forests corrupted by infernal magic: nature itself twisted and weaponized. Unlike human zombies, the bear zombie retains some of the original predatory instinct, making it unpredictable and brutally effective in open spaces.

variantes.supervivencia: His mace is devastating: one blow can fell an unprepared warrior. Keep your distance and attack him with magic or projectiles. His low AC makes him easy to hit, but his Undead Fortitude can save him once.
variantes.habilidad: Like the basic zombie, it can survive a lethal blow with a CON roll. His Large size allows him to sweep multiple targets with his mace in a single bonus action.
variantes.lore: When a necromancer doesn't have enough human corpses, he turns to the remains of ogres: huge, tough, easy to control. An ogre zombie can carry tons of supplies, knock down dungeon doors, or serve as a living battering ram in a siege. Its slowness is its only real flaw.

variantes.habitat: Corrupted Marshes, Cursed Forests, Underworld Tunnels
variantes.supervivencia: USE FIRE OR ACID. The troll's regeneration is suppressed by death, but its supernatural constitution makes it extremely difficult to destroy without those elements. Without fire, he can stand up again and again.
variantes.habilidad: The regeneration of the original troll is suppressed but not eliminated. With no fire or acid damage in the round, he recovers 5 HP at the start of his turn even if he is at 0. He only dies permanently with fire or radiant.
variantes.lore: Killing a troll is already difficult in life. Reanimating is one of the costliest mistakes a novice necromancer can make. Necrotic magic does not remove the troll's supernatural resilience, it only partially numbs it. The result is a creature that looks dead but refuses to be, crawling back with rotting claws even after taking blows that would kill any other undead.

variantes.habitat: Lairs of Fallen Beholders, Deep Dungeons
variantes.supervivencia: Its eye beams are random but deadly: it can paralyze, disintegrate, or drain magic in a single turn. Stay moving and use cover. Unlike a living beholder, it cannot use the central Antimagic Ray.
variantes.habilidad: At the beginning of each turn he shoots 1d6 random rays from his side eyes: Paralyzing, Terrifying, Disintegrating, Slowing, Draining or Telekinesis. Without conscious control, lightning bolts shoot in all directions.
variantes.lore: When a beholder dies and a necromancer collects his remains, he gains one of the most erratic and unpredictable weapons in the undead arsenal. The beholder zombie does not think, does not aim with intent and does not distinguish between friend and enemy. Its rays shoot randomly in all directions, turning the room it inhabits into a zone of pure death. There have been entire expeditions destroyed by the friendly fire of these monsters.

variantes.habitat: Desecrated Dragon Lairs, Cursed Mountain Peaks
variantes.resistente: Poison (Immune), varies depending on the original dragon
variantes.supervivencia: His breath is still lethal although weakened. Treat each encounter as if the dragon were alive: take cover before it exhales. On land he is clumsy; If you can lock to the ground with spells you negate its biggest advantage.
variantes.habilidad: Retains original but weakened dragon's breath weapon (damage halved, DC reduced). Recharge in 2 turns. Its Huge size allows it to sweep multiple enemies with its tail as a bonus action.
variantes.lore: The zombie dragon is the darkest trophy that a powerful necromancer can hold. Reanimating a dragon requires not only arcane power but also access to its intact lair, its bones still connected, and weeks of rituals. The result preserves the dragon's imposing form, its destructive breath and its ability to fly, but none of its intelligence or pride. Obey in silence, without ambition, without fear. A perfect tool for a teacher willing to do anything.

mimic.supervivencia: Don't touch anything that looks too clean. If a chest has no dust, it is a Mimic. Hit it before trying to open it; It is better to break the lock than lose a hand.
mimic.habilidad: As long as it remains motionless using the copied form, the Mimic is logically invisible at the perceptual level (indistinguishable from a normal object). It secretes a powerful natural sticky polymer that completely covers its entire altered body; Any creature or object that touches it directly will automatically become attached and Severely Grappled (Strength DC 13). All of your impact attack rolls against grapples stuck to your body have Unbreakable Direct Advantage.
mimic.lore: Ingenious and unpredictable amorphous monomaniacal predators curiously born from dust and latent magic in forgotten corners. They acquire with terrifying ease the solid, textured and identical consistency of almost any common inert object, commonly disguising their voracious corpulent figure of monstrosity as majestic trunks, antique shelves or heavy wooden doors to ambush unsuspecting explorers in carved dungeons. The raw, unwary or careless greed of others becomes the great lethal bait as they become fatally trapped in outstretched arms or uselessly clutched swords, while deadly surprise jaws spring forth to chew them and swallow them alive for perpetual painful lamentation.

basilisco.supervivencia: Never look into his eyes. If you don't have a mirror to see your reflection, attack blindly or trust your ears. His breath is fetid, but his gaze is the true end.
basilisco.habilidad: His main terror lies in his lethal eyes of magical influence. If a creature starts its turn within 30 feet and the basilisk looks at it with uncovered eyes, the target must make a brutal Constitution save (DC 12). Upon failing, he begins to turn into rock, becoming magically restricted in speed, and a second failure on his next turn completely seals the individual's transformation into solid stone permanently.
basilisco.lore: This fearsome reptilian monstrosity armed with heavy, robust legs hunts guided exclusively by its deadly stone-like gaze rather than using its thick fangs to feed. They frequently inhabit arid rocky areas or desolate depths of dark cave systems, where their lair is commonly ill-omened by the alarming and disturbing overabundance of incredibly precise 'stone statues' of local animals, or frightened adventurers. Remote rumors from learned arcanists tell that a delicate oil solution extracted from the foul basal gastric sac of the fallen basilisk itself can temporarily reverse the curse of lethal immobility on an unfortunate soul frozen upon being anointed.

cubo_gelatinoso.supervivencia: Don't try to hit it with metal weapons; use fire magic to make it explode. If you manage to get him out of the dungeon, his body will quickly melt.
cubo_gelatinoso.habilidad: At first glance, under the normal lighting conditions of an underground conduit, the presence of the Cube wall requires visually noticing the deception with Constantly High Wisdom (Perception DC 15). As it advances head-on without braking through space, it ruthlessly subdues creatures, engulfing them under a wave of heavy soft mass (Dexterity Save DC 12). Any trapped creature will be dragged under constant acid damage (3d6), suffering strong organic imprisonment, making it impossible to breathe freely.
cubo_gelatinoso.lore: These strange and feared unusual predators without reasoning biologically adopt their strange geometric quadrangular shape adapted to millimeter accuracy to sweep the floors, completely filling from end to end the narrow alleys of claustrophobic cavernous dungeons. They completely lack either the slightest bit of malice, pity or real tactical intelligence of the living dead. Their actions are eternally comparable to those of mere slow but deadly garbage collectors who absorb all organic impudence. Due to a metabolic failure, the silver metallic armor of previous disintegrated warriors and priceless golden gleaming treasures will resist the translucent gelatinous stomachs, paradoxically acting as the ironic ultimate lethal bait of hypnotizing floating attraction in the darkness that will alert lethargic stunned bandits of their impending doom.

ankheg.supervivencia: Don't let it catch you in its jaws; once he does, he will pour acid into your wounds. If you hear vibrations under your feet, run toward rocky terrain.
ankheg.habilidad: The Ankheg's jaws are capable of ensnaring a creature and crushing it while exuding corrosive enzymes. As a last resort, he can launch a powerful line of stomach acid to melt his enemies' armor from a distance.
ankheg.lore: Monstrous and voracious insects that inhabit grasslands and forests, excavating extensive networks of tunnels a few meters below the fertile surface. They rarely venture outside their dens, preferring to lie in wait and feel the ground vibrations produced by a horse or an unwary traveler. When they attack, they suddenly emerge with relentless fury, seeking to drag their prey into the subterranean darkness.

dragon_rojo.supervivencia: Never enter his treasure without a ring of fire resistance. The heat from its scales will melt your steel before you can touch it. Attack from the flanks and ignore their arrogance; His tongue is as sharp as his claws.
dragon_rojo.habilidad: A burst of liquid fire that can melt stone itself in seconds. Only warriors anointed with titan blood have managed to get close without being consumed.
dragon_rojo.lore: Undisputed monarchs among the scaly wyrms, motivated by colossal arrogance rivaled only by the grandeur of their golden accumulations. A Red Dragon doesn't just burn cities with tides of fire; They subjugate kingdoms demanding bloody tithes because they are perceived as the magnum perfection of the natural environment. Battling them means recklessly crashing into bone-melting fire and draconic primordial magic.

dragon_negro.supervivencia: Water sources near their lair will be corrupted, so bring your own supplies. Maintain wide distances to prevent multiple allies from being hit by his line of acid breath, and prepare to deal with the blinding cloud of insects.
dragon_negro.habilidad: The dragon exhales a powerful jet of acid in a line 27 m long. Consumes both armor and flesh, dealing lethal damage.
dragon_negro.lore: Elder black dragons delight in the suffering and ruin of entire kingdoms. They seek magic that allows them to corrupt the land and treasure tainted symbols of hope and relics of fallen empires. The mere presence of this beast transforms deplorable swamps into places infested with horrors and harmful magic.

dragon_azul.supervivencia: The regions near their lair are filled with treacherous sinkholes and plagued by blinding dust storms. The dragon can fly completely invisibly, so relying on vision is not enough; Prepare for surprise attacks and sonic booms before you hear the thunder.
dragon_azul.habilidad: The dragon exhales withering lightning in a line 36 m long. Additionally, he is innately proficient at casting spells to turn himself invisible or shatter illusions with deafening sonic booms.
dragon_azul.lore: Arrogant and imperious, blue dragons are formidable tyrants who crave control and rule through networks of subjugated followers, sects, and criminal networks. Converting large expanses of desert and abandoned ruins into their fortifications, they transform their vast domains into dictatorial empires. They thesaurize masterpieces of art, fallen emblems of government and diametrically repudiate everything they consider vulgar or imperfect.

lich.supervivencia: Don't try to kill him if you haven't found his phylactery first. The Lich will return eternally as long as its essence is bound to this world. Use light magic to prevent it from draining your soul.
lich.habilidad: A magician who has cheated death through dark rituals. His arcane power is comparable to that of the gods.
lich.lore: Sorcerers and arcane masters who refused to fade into oblivion, binding their souls to a phylactery through arcane desecration. A Lich perfects forbidden dark magics and builds deadly dungeons or controls empires by pulling strings behind royalty. These immortals plan their stratagems across millennia; Taking down his physical form is hardly a minor setback until you find the mysterious receptacle of his corrupted soul and destroy it.

tarrasque.resistente: All non-magical damage, Fire, Poison, Magic (Reflection)
tarrasque.supervivencia: Don't try to kill him; just try to survive. Its shell reflects spells back to the caster. The only documented way to stop it is to put it into a state of deep torpor using 9th level magic or pure wish. If it roars, the world trembles.
tarrasque.habilidad_titulo: Reflecting Shell, Engulf and Dread Presence
tarrasque.habilidad: His Reflecting Shell deflects without damage or has a 16% (1 on the d6 die) to return any spell aimed at it, magic projectile, or line spell back to the caster. It has Advantage against any magical save. Its attacks allow it to Engulf its prey (up to Large size), confining them to its stomach where they suffer 16d6 acid damage per turn. Its Dread Presence requires a DC 17 Wisdom save at 36 yards or suffer continued terrifying panic.
tarrasque.lore: The incarnation of the end of times, the cataclysmic beast whose name terrifies the immortals. The Tarrasque is a machine of inescapable destruction that spends centuries dormant at the core of the world. When an ancient hunger awakens him, nothing blooms where he steps. Entire kingdoms have attempted to stop their advance, only adding shattered armies to their teeth. An avatar of absolute ruin and incomprehensible instinct, whose brutal strength is sinisterly surpassed by a powerful magical shell that rejects and drastically nullifies the attacks of the elite sorcerers fallen at its feet.

beholder.supervivencia: Don't try to attack the beholder head-on; Its central eye nullifies magic. Attack from the flanks and try to blind its eyestalks before it fires its death or disintegration rays.
beholder.habilidad: The Beholder's enormous frontal eye emits an invisible cone of constant antimagical energy. As long as it remains open, any spell, magical item, or arcane effect trapped within that field is absolutely suppressed and unusable.
beholder.lore: The erratic and nightmarish observer of the underground. A macabre orb crowned with eyestalks simultaneously aiming and besieging from disintegration to mortal terror. A being ruled by extreme paranoia; His distorted perception deceives him into deducing that the immensity of the universe and any alien species seek to sully his unattainable perfect genetic design.

kraken.supervivencia: Don't fight him in the water if you don't have powerful lightning magic. Their tentacles can wrap around your ship and sink it in seconds. Look for the central eye, it's his only real vulnerable point.
kraken.habilidad: A being of ancient intelligence that can sink entire fleets with a single movement of its tentacles.
kraken.lore: Primeval lords of the deep abyss, who once ruled over the terrestrial creation with an implacable fist. A Kraken has colossal strength to tear apart leviathans like rotten wood, while warping the weather at will with dense storms and blinding lightning. Inhuman intelligences that inhabit coral labyrinths waiting prophetic hours to return and recover their forgotten terrestrial empire by submerging entire continents.

balor.supervivencia: Don't try to put out his fire; It is part of its essence. The only way to defeat a Balor is to keep your distance and use ranged holy energy attacks. And be careful: his final explosion upon death can wipe out everything around him.
balor.habilidad: A general of the demonic hordes, engulfed in flames and wielding a fire whip. His very presence corrupts the earth.
balor.lore: Supreme marshals and champions of the abyssal armies wielding the scourge of their imminent sulfur wrath. These titans measure dozens of feet wrapped in unquenchable fire. His runeblade of desolation turns impenetrable armor into molten scrap. They do not tolerate failure and when physically struck down they explode suddenly, simulating thermonuclear detonations, ensuring indiscriminate destruction.

vampiro_ancestral.supervivencia: Don't let his blood caress touch you; It will drain your vitality and memories. Use holy light to avoid his mist form and don't trust anyone inside his castle.
vampiro_ancestral.habilidad: A noble of the night who has ruled his domain for millennia. His charisma is as lethal as his fangs.
vampiro_ancestral.lore: The first children of the night. These cursed nobles have ruled from the shadows for millennia, weaving plots that dethrone kings and consume entire bloodlines. Unlike a simple blood drinker, an Ancestral Vampire perceives the ages as mere temporal seasons and masters lost magical arts. His hypnotic charisma conceals the primordial beast; They rarely enter combat by brute force, but if they do, they unleash insatiable carnage worthy of legend.

bugbears.supervivencia: Don't underestimate them because of their size; His muscular strength is overwhelming. Bugbears are experts at stealth and surprise attacks. Look carefully before entering a dark cave.
bugbears.habilidad: If the Bugbear manages to surprise a creature and hit it with a physical attack during the first turn of a fight, the hit deals additional devastating damage (usually an extra 2d6).
bugbears.lore: The older, deadly cousins ​​of the goblin lineage. These towering assassins easily stand over seven feet tall and are topped with muscular bodies, but their thick, hispid coat of fur conceals an unnatural capacity for absolute stealth and undetectable strides. Bugbears are lazy by nature when they are not torturing or raiding minor villages. Unlike the noisy and chaotic orc armies, a Bugbear will hunt, gliding silently through the blackness before suddenly swooping in with an old serrated mace to strangle and snap the necks of distracted guards in the early hours of the morning.

gnolls.supervivencia: Do not attack them head on if they are in a pack; His laughter is the harbinger of a coordinated attack. Use area magic to disperse his horde before engaging in melee combat.
gnolls.habilidad: When a Gnoll reduces a living creature to 0 hit points with a melee attack, the manic excitement of the slaughter allows it to immediately lunge at the next prey in a lethal frenzy and unleash an additional ferocious bite.
gnolls.lore: Horrifying hyena-headed humanoids created by the vile influence of Yeenoghu, the Lord of the Hunger Demons. Unlike orc or goblin tribes, Gnolls do not build settlements, farm, or forge trading alliances; They are the very embodiment of a destructive itinerant gluttony. Massive packs sweep across the grasslands and villages in a cacophony of hysterical laughter and demonic madness. After their victorious passage they leave no prisoners and much less corpses; The gnolls break the bones of the fallen to suck the marrow and devour the carrion in blood feasts, leaving nothing but stained lands and silence behind them.

lizardfolk.supervivencia: Don't attack them in the water; They are expert swimmers. Attack them from dry ground and use cold magic to reduce their agility before engaging in combat.
lizardfolk.habilidad: Their pragmatism is so brutal that in brief moments of rest they can bleed a corpse and carve shields, javelins, and blowguns using exclusively the ribs, skin, and spines of their fallen enemies. In combat, its jaws tear apart flesh, completely ignoring pain or pleas.
lizardfolk.lore: An ancient reptilian people who inhabit the most treacherous swamps and sweltering jungles in the world. For an average humanoid, it is impossible to reason with a Lizardfolk using morality: they have absolutely no empathy, fear, or emotional pity. They experience the world through the prism of strict utilitarianism and cold survival; If you die on their lands, they will not see a tragedy, but rather fresh nutrients and resources to forge new bone weapons. Although they are not inherently malicious or sadistic creatures, their calculating intellect and alien coldness make them terrifying adversaries to those who invade their flooded domain.

doppelganger.habitat: Cities, Royal Courts, Taverns and Dark Alleys
doppelganger.supervivencia: Don't trust your own allies if they've been alone for too long. Always establish passwords or secret greetings with your group before entering suspicious areas. And be careful: a Doppelganger reads your superficial thoughts instinctively, so it will know exactly the answer you expect to hear if you try to ask it a trick question.
doppelganger.habilidad: This sinister creature can biologically mold its flesh to organically and identically replicate the appearance, voice, and even basic clothing of any humanoid it has ever seen. This is magically complemented by his gift of reading superficial minds, appropriating recent memories or expected reactions to perform impeccable and indistinguishable imitations.
doppelganger.lore: In its true, pristine form, a Doppelganger is a macabre being: a slender humanoid figure, with grayish, hairless skin, almost completely lacking in distinctive facial features. However, witnessing this state is almost impossible, as they are the undisputed masters of infiltration and subterfuge. Operating similarly to social parasites, they do not have societies or kingdoms of their own; They subsist by invading the cultures of other races by taking over the lives and identities of influential nobles, guards, or even local heroes. Under cover of the trust they steal, they are capable of orchestrating coups d'état or plunging entire families into absolute paranoia, destroying them from within without needing to shed a single drop of blood in direct combat.

rust_monster.supervivencia: Don't use metal weapons or armor if you don't want to lose them forever. Use wooden sticks, stones or pure magic. If you get close, its mere presence will rust your belongings in seconds.
rust_monster.habilidad: Their antennae secrete a chemical that instantly oxidizes any ferrous metal on contact: swords, armor, and shields disintegrate in seconds. It can detect metal through stone walls from over 30 feet away, making it an unstoppable predator within dungeons. Even inadvertent rubbing against its shell can damage the edge of a quality weapon.
rust_monster.lore: Few beings on all planes generate as much panic among veteran adventurers as the Rust Monster. A fully armored warrior who has survived dragons can be left defenseless in seconds against this harmless-looking creature. Their origin is debated: some arcane theories hold that they were deliberately created by underground wizards to protect their treasure chambers from looters, while others consider them a natural evolution of insects exposed to veins of alchemical mineral. Whatever their origin, they are feared by miners, heroes, and merchants alike. They don't kill for pleasure; They just feed. But leaving your gear in rust dust before facing the rest of a dungeon can be just as effective a death sentence.

bestia_tremula.vulnerable: Great dependence on her vision (Blinding her nullifies her illusion)
bestia_tremula.supervivencia: Don't try to attack the panther you're seeing, because it's not there. Use area spells or try throwing sand in his eyes; If you manage to blind it, the beast will not be able to project its illusory form and will once again be a normal target.
bestia_tremula.habilidad: Her fur generates a constant magical refraction, projecting an optical illusion of herself one meter from her true position. It attacks by lashing out with two thick tentacles that grow from its shoulders and end in spiked pads that destroy flesh.
bestia_tremula.lore: Originating from the enigmatic realms of the Feywild, Shivering Beasts are macabre felines resembling large, blue-black panthers that walk silently on six muscular legs. The creature is cursed or blessed with a fey gift: a permanent illusion that makes it appear to always be slightly moved from its true location, allowing swords and arrows to pass through it without harming it. Those unfortunate enough to come across one rarely live to tell the tale, as they are brutally lashed and torn to death by the beast's formidable thorny tentacles.

phase_spider.supervivencia: Don't let him take you to the Ethereal Plane alone. Use 'See the Invisible' magic to anticipate his dimension jumps and attack right after he loses his mist form.
phase_spider.habilidad: As a bonus action, the Phase Spider can instantly move from the Material Plane to the Ethereal Plane, or vice versa. It will usually materialize behind its enemy's back to attack with forceful ferocity, injecting a torrid lethal (CON DC 11) paralyzing poison. A very dangerous trait is that if you reduce a creature's HP to zero with poison, it will be left in stable remorse, deeply paralyzed for full hours before being dragged into the void.
phase_spider.lore: Phase Spiders are loathsome aberrations entrenched interdimensionally upon the thin dimensional membrane that separates mortal planes from ethereal universes of shadow and mist. Distinguished by their six glowing violet eyeballs detecting vulnerable souls through the veil, they do not spend their energies making cobwebs. Their gloomy nature lies in being absolute itinerant hunters: an adventurer will believe he is walking through a silent empty tunnel feeling protected by rear armor, but will end up brutally poisoned before even managing to see the jaws that jumped between dimensions, piercing his spine and abducting him to undocumented realms to consume him with sinister parsimony.

treant.supervivencia: Don't try to fight the Trent without fire; It's his only real weakness. Attack from the roots and use heavy axes if you want to survive its cold oak branches.
treant.habilidad: He can awaken up to two normal trees within a 60-foot radius, turning them into allies that attack and block his enemies from passing for hours. Additionally, his stomp shakes the ground over a wide area, knocking anyone who is not heavy or stable enough to their feet. Their branches act as colossal maces capable of crushing shields and bruising plate armor.
treant.lore: Treants are the embodiment of the living memory of the primordial forests. They have existed since before the elves laid their first trails, and have witnessed the birth and collapse of entire empires with the calm indifference of someone who measures time in centuries. They attack not out of aggression but out of sacred duty: when uncontrolled logging, fire, or dark magic threaten their grove, the ground shakes and the oaks come to life. An angry Trent is a moving catastrophe. However, druids and forest-abiding travelers know that a Treant can be the most faithful ally imaginable, an eternal guardian who remembers every name and crime ever committed under its canopy.

variantes.supervivencia: Fire terrifies them and gives them a disadvantage. Lightning, on the other hand, heals and revitalizes them. Use forceful attacks to break its seams.
variantes.habilidad: Any lightning damage you take heals you instead of damaging you. Fire damage causes fear, preventing you from attacking effectively on your next turn.
variantes.lore: A mass of corpse parts sewn together with copper threads and animated by a spark of elemental life. The Flesh Golem is not an undead, but a parody of life created by alchemical science and magic. It lacks a soul, but possesses brute strength that responds blindly to its creator's commands, as long as it is not frightened by the flames.

variantes.supervivencia: The weapons stay stuck to his body. Fire makes it solid and brittle, facilitating its destruction. Prevent it from engulfing you.
variantes.habilidad: Any non-magical weapon that hits it has a chance to become stuck. It can attempt to engulf a small or medium-sized enemy, suffocating it inside.
variantes.lore: A shapeless mass that barely maintains bipedalism. The Mud Golem is an inexpensive but effective defense, capable of stopping intruders by simply trapping them in its own malleable mass until they surrender or die.

variantes.supervivencia: Its body deforms with blows, absorbing impacts. Heals acid damage. If he goes into a frenzy, he becomes much faster, don't try to run away then.
variantes.habilidad: He can enter a state of haste that doubles his attacks for a short period. Their blows reduce the target's maximum hit points due to the living clay curse.
variantes.lore: Sculpted from blessed clay and endowed with a precarious life through scrolls of sacred parchment inserted into his mouth. Clay Golems are prone to losing control if their delicate magical balance is broken, becoming machines of destruction that do not know friend from foe.

variantes.supervivencia: Use sound attacks to fracture it. Avoid light spells or magical projectiles, as they will reflect them back at you. It is fragile but hits with precision cuts.
variantes.habilidad: Has a 50% chance to reflect magic projectiles and radiant damage. Upon receiving critical damage, it explodes into fragments that wound nearby attackers.
variantes.lore: Made of pure arcane crystals that act as lenses for the energy of the radiant plane. Crystal Golems are beautiful and deadly, often used by archmages not only for defense, but as accumulators of magical energy for their most ambitious experiments.

variantes.supervivencia: His aura freezes the ground, making movement difficult. Fire is your best option; weakens him and reduces his armor. Their blows can freeze equipment.
variantes.habilidad: Create an area of ​​difficult movement around you. Can launch a blast of ice that briefly paralyzes and deals intense cold damage.
variantes.lore: Sculpted in eternal ice from the deepest glaciers. Ice Golems are guardians of the northern kingdoms, almost invisible in the middle of a blizzard, waiting for the heat of an intruder to reveal their position to attack with the precision of an icicle.

variantes.supervivencia: His body is fluid; The arrows pass through him. Water makes it heavy and slow. Beware of its blinding sandstorm.
variantes.habilidad_titulo: Fluid Shape and Veil of Powder
variantes.habilidad: It can pass through tiny openings. Creates a cloud of sand around him that blinds enemies and gives him an advantage in evasion.
variantes.lore: Children of the dunes, these golems are the terror of the caravans. Able to dissolve into a pile of ordinary sand and reform in an instant behind their enemies, they are the invisible assassins of the desert.

variantes.supervivencia: Don't attack him with arrows; It is ineffective. Mace damage breaks their bones easily. His aura drains the life from the dying.
variantes.habilidad: Heals by killing creatures. His body is covered in sharp fragments that return part of the damage received in melee.
variantes.lore: Unlike a skeleton, the Bone Golem is an architectural structure of human remains. Thousands of bones fused by dark magic create an entity that does not rest, does not feel and whose only goal is to add more pieces to its own form.

variantes.supervivencia: It's slow but relentless. His aura of slowness makes fighting him like moving underwater. Use stone destruction magic or heavy weapons.
variantes.habilidad: Alternates between normal attacks and a magical pulse that slows all nearby enemies, reducing their speed and number of actions by half.
variantes.lore: Carved from a single block of granite or basalt, these sentinels are the standard of magical defense. A Stone Golem can remain motionless for centuries, looking like a decorative statue, until an intruder activates its guard protocol, at which point the ground trembles under its stone tread.

variantes.supervivencia: Don't touch it with bare hands. Cold damage solidifies him, increasing his AC but reducing his speed to zero. Explodes upon death.
variantes.habilidad: It damages anyone who hits it in melee. Upon death, its core overheats and explodes into a large area of ​​fire and molten rock.
variantes.lore: A lava river with a humanoid shape. Magma Golems are unstable and extremely dangerous, existing only in places of unbearable heat where their liquid form can keep flowing.

variantes.supervivencia: Don't cast spells directly on it; absorbs them to enhance his own attacks. Attack physically with powerful weapons to deplete your mana reserve.
variantes.habilidad: Absorbs the level of any spell cast nearby. When its reservoir is full, it releases a burst of pure energy that damages everyone in the area.
variantes.lore: Etched with every syllable of the ancient alphabet, Rune Golems are the living processors of magic. It is said that if a Rune Golem is destroyed correctly, the secrets of the universe can be read in its fragments... if one survives the arcane explosion.

variantes.supervivencia: Don't waste fire; craziness. Use adamantine weapons to penetrate its armor. Beware of its poisonous gas breath.
variantes.habilidad: Heals with fire damage. Releases a cloud of lethal poison gas in a 5 meter area every few turns.
variantes.lore: The pinnacle of construction engineering. Forged in the forges of the lower planes, Iron Golems are living tanks capable of laying waste to entire platoons. His body is a fortress unto itself, imbued with a cold, mechanical malevolence.

variantes.habitat: Planes of Fire, Solid Magma Chambers
variantes.supervivencia: It is extremely sharp; Hitting it usually results in cuts for the attacker. Blunt damage can fracture it, but watch out for flying splinters.
variantes.habilidad: Any melee attacker takes damage from contact with its sharp edges. He has significant innate resistance to low-level spells.
variantes.lore: Forged at the point where lava meets the magical void. The Obsidian Golem is a lethal jewel, a guardian that combines the hardness of the stone with the sharpness of the purest crystal.

hag.supervivencia: Don't make deals with them; You will always lose more than you win. Attack them separately; A coven of witches is exponentially more lethal than a single witch.
hag.habilidad: Hags can cover themselves with an illusion to appear as kind old women.
hag.lore: Ancient and repulsive weavers of misfortunes and mortal contracts that live in the most putrid corners of the swamps. Always fleeing from their own misery, witches use sinister illusions to adopt false beauty or simulate compassionate fragility. They fiercely despise other people's happiness and pure goodness; Its only delight consists in corrupting the human heart, demanding macabre payments for poisoned favors: tears of a firstborn, the last breath of a saint or memories of love. Gathered in unholy covens, their arcane power rivals the worst of curses.

vecna.habitat: Towers of Eternity, Planes of Shadow
vecna.supervivencia: Don't try to hide anything; Vecna ​​already knows your secrets. Use evil protection magic and search for the lost artifacts of the gods if you want to stand a chance. If you die in his presence, your soul will belong to him forever.
vecna.habilidad: Vecna ​​can paralyze his enemies by revealing truths that their minds cannot process.
vecna.lore: The Master of Secrets, the Lich Deity. Vecna ​​not only ruled dead empires, but transcended life to reign over forbidden whispers. Once a mortal magician, he climbed to divinity by snatching destiny from the hands of the elder gods. Now, secret cults across the plane plot their machinations, seeking to reunite his lost Eye and Hand. Facing it is not fighting against a physical being, but rather battling against the dark secrets that sustain reality itself.

tiamat.supervivencia: Don't try to fight Tiamat with just one head. Each head has its own breath and each must be defeated separately. Don't trust his mercy; it doesn't have any.
tiamat.habilidad: Its five heads act independently: Red (cone of fire, DC 27), Blue (ray of lightning, DC 27), Green (cone of poison, DC 27), White (cone of cold, DC 27) and Black (line of acid, DC 27). He can use up to three different breaths in a single turn as part of his Multiattack. Additionally, each head can react with a bite (damage 2d10+10) as a reaction action if the corresponding head has not yet attacked that turn. His legendary actions allow him to attack, use a breath, or reposition himself without spending his main turn.
tiamat.lore: The Dragon Queen, chromatic majesty in all its terrible glory. Tiamat lies captive in the Nine Hells, but her fury shakes the earth itself. Its five heads represent the primordial chromatic dragons (red, green, blue, white and black), and its sects seek the ritual to free it. If this winged deity were to cross the veil of our reality, entire continents would burn in an endless storm of frost, poison, lightning, acid, and eternal flames.

asmodeus.supervivencia: Do not try to fight Asmodeus with weapons. His greatest power is not his mace, but his tongue. If you enter their domain, you are already under a contract. Only a divine oath from a God of Justice can break his will.
asmodeus.habilidad: The embodiment of evil order and the ruler of the Nine Hells. His mere presence corrupts the souls of mortals.
asmodeus.lore: The Supreme Father and undisputed Archduke of Lawful Evil, the infallible Architect of the Nine Hells. It usually assumes human presence of divine grace, however, Asmodeus is the eternal manifestation of cosmic sin. He tempts purity with dark insidious contracts, weaving the final web. The deifics fear him deeply due to the lethal mathematical patience with which he schemes to dictate the falls from the dawn of the multiverse.

nightwalker.supervivencia: Do not attempt to combat a Nightwalker without a powerful holy light. His aura drains your maximum vitality permanently. If his shadow caress touches you, your soul will cease to exist.
nightwalker.habilidad: Any living creature within 30 feet has its maximum health permanently reduced.
nightwalker.lore: Unspeakable silhouettes forged from emptiness within the inhospitable Shadow Plane. The Nightwalker arises when brave hopes drown, overwhelmed by negative entropy. Its vast corpulence darkens and radiates a dead pernicious aura that freezes the light itself. They persist only by and for the only dark universal instinct: to irreversibly eradicate organic souls without leaving the slightest stain or fleshy residue.

demilich.supervivencia: Don't try to reason with him or use mind control magic. The Demilich devours souls to regenerate. Its howl stops the heart; use silencing spells if you can.
demilich.habilidad: The Demilich lets out a spectral howl. All creatures within 30 feet must succeed on a Constitution save.
demilich.lore: As a Lich's intellect travels to incomprehensible reaches of the multiverse, its body abandons its material anchor and crumbles to dust. The only thing left is a floating gem-encrusted skull. Passionless, a Demilich concentrates lethal magic of desolation condensed into his spectral form. Their howls instantly rip out the souls of their victims, trapping them in their glowing crystals in perpetual torment. He's less of an undead and more of a cosmic curse.

elder_brain.supervivencia: Don't try to reason with him; His telepathy will flood your mind with madness. The Elder Brain controls the environment in the same way he controls his servants.
elder_brain.habilidad: All creatures within 120 feet must succeed on an Intelligence save.
elder_brain.lore: A bulging brain beating slowly inside a bubbling pool, the unquestionable peak of the Mind Flayers. His reprehensible intellect operates by processing telekinetic calculations to control underground hives. Plot, in asynchrony and lethality against surface empires, the complete restructuring of the world by absorbing alien minds for the absolute benefit of its blind armies.

yeti.supervivencia: Fire is your best weapon; His fur burns easily and it terrifies him. Keep an eye out for blizzards, as its natural camouflage makes it invisible in the snow.
yeti.habilidad: The Yeti can fix its gaze on a creature. If the target fails its Constitution save, it is paralyzed by icy, blood-curdling fear.
yeti.lore: A large humanoid covered in thick white fur that hunts on the highest peaks. Their strength is abysmal and they delight in the fresh meat of adventurers lost in the snow.

duergar.supervivencia: Don't trust your eyes, they can become invisible at will. Avoid fighting them in the dark, their superior vision and ambush tactics are lethal.
duergar.habilidad: The Duergar has the innate ability to turn its body invisible for a short period and also double its magical size, gaining destructive strength and endurance.
duergar.lore: Dwarves scarred by countless ages in the darkness of the Underdark. Severe and cold-hearted smiths, they possess inherent magic resulting from the cruel influence of their environment and former masters.

mind_flayer.supervivencia: Never face them in battles of mental exhaustion. His psychic blast stuns the area; keep the formation spread out. If they manage to latch onto your head, you have mere seconds before they extract your brain tissue.
mind_flayer.habilidad: Once its facial tentacles squeeze the skull of an incapacitated prey, the Mindslayer sucks and devours the brain marrow, causing instant death and absorbing the victim's memories.
mind_flayer.lore: Heirs to an extradimensional empire that once enslaved countless worlds. The Illithids, or Mind Scourges, are humanoids with purple skin and faces crowned by tentacles that feed exclusively on the frontal lobes of intelligent beings. They deeply despise all surface races as mere nutritious livestock. They subdue their prey using relentless telepathic assaults that nullify the will before laying their tentacles into them. They operate from labyrinthine underground colonies in a perpetual hive, mentally linked to the Elder Brain who dictates each of their sadistic mathematical movements.

oso_lechuza.supervivencia: It is one of the beasts with the least impulse control that exists. If you find her protecting her territory or her young, she will fight to the death. Its bite breaks torsos and its claws tear shields; Attack her from a distance and don't corner her.
oso_lechuza.habilidad: It combines the excessive strength and heavy clawing of a wounded bear with the privileged vision and cervical rotation of an owl, making it almost impossible to suffer a successful night ambush.
oso_lechuza.lore: A monstrous aberrant hybrid conceived, according to old legends, as the product of the cruel experiments of a crazed wizard. The Owlbear has the muscular body of a large ursid, but with the head, thick plumage and sharp beak of a colossal owl. They are notoriously short-tempered and extremely territorial. Once this predator smells your blood and lets out its distinctive, guttural screech through the blackness of the dense forest, little will stop its furious, deadly frontal charge.

aboleth.habitat: Underground Depths, Lakes of the Underdark
aboleth.supervivencia: Don't let their tentacles touch you. Its mucus will transform your skin into a translucent membrane that dissolves in the air, forcing you to live underwater or die from suffocation on the surface.
aboleth.habilidad_titulo: Psychic Slavery and Disease of the Depth
aboleth.habilidad: In addition to its telepathic power to subjugate minds, the Aboleth excretes a lethal mucus. Whoever is injured by its tentacles suffers an irreversible mutation that prevents them from breathing out of the water after a few hours.
aboleth.lore: Amphibious beings that look like grotesque prehistoric triocular fish that dominated the world's oceans long before the gods intervened in creation. Aboleths possess one of the most terrifying characteristics in the multiverse: perfect genetic memory. Each individual perfectly remembers the wisdom of his ancestors from the beginning of time, as well as the recorded memory of all the offenses committed by the divine pantheon against him. They wait patiently in underground lakes, plotting their cold vengeance and adding entire mortal civilizations to their legions of hypnotized slaves.

troll.supervivencia: Never set out to hunt a Troll without a burning torch or vials of acid. It doesn't matter if you amputate his arms or cut off his head; If you don't burn the stumps, it will regenerate the limbs or the limb will live on its own to attack you.
troll.habilidad: Unless it takes fire or acid damage on the last turn, the Troll's warped flesh heals its wounds at a visible, almost repulsive rate.
troll.lore: Relentless predators of enormous proportions, born with an incessant hunger that devours any organic matter that crosses their path. The Troll usually has disgusting green rubbery skin and asymmetrical or disproportionate limbs, due to the countless times it has lost body parts that grow back irregularly. They feel no real pain and completely lack the instinct for self-preservation; Only the sight of a flaming torch is capable of causing them genuine panic, an instinct rooted in the fact that the flame is the only thing that nullifies their regenerative mutation.

slaad.supervivencia: Never let yourself be scratched or bitten without receiving magical healing immediately. Their attacks can implant eggs in your body that will hatch, eating you from the inside, or give you a disease that will slowly and painfully transform you into one of them.
slaad.habilidad: The Slaad's claws and fangs convey the pure essence of Limbo's Chaos. They can use their victims as living incubators or infect them so that they mutate, perpetuating their bizarre, alien species.
slaad.lore: Hailing from the stormy and unstable plane of Limbo, the Slaads are monstrous aberrations of batracian appearance and deeply unpredictable nature. Driven by an instinctive need to spread chaos and their own species, they attack savagely and without apparent logic. Their reproductive cycle is the terror of scholars and adventurers: some castes implant eggs under the skin of living hosts, while others spread a deadly mutagenic virus. Their mutant and regenerative anatomy, combined with their relentless savagery, make them formidable adversaries. There is no way to reason with a being whose very existence is an aberration from the natural order.

behir.vulnerable: Large size makes it an easy target outdoors
behir.resistente: Immune to Lightning or Poison Damage
behir.supervivencia: Avoid narrow hallways where his lightning breath has nowhere to dissipate. If it lunges at you, prioritize keeping your distance: if it bites you, you will use its muscular rings to immobilize you and it will not stop squeezing you until you break your bones.
behir.habilidad: It builds up massive static energy in its lungs to exhale a devastating, elongated line of lightning. Additionally, it uses its enormous serpentine body and twelve claws (on its six legs) to crush and suffocate giants and unwary alike, before swallowing them whole.
behir.lore: The Behir is a terrifying predator more than 12 meters long and heavy like a huge rock. Similar to an armored snake that crawls at enormous speed with its six strong legs, it is equipped with thick horns pointing backwards on its head. Ancient legends maintain that these aberrant monstrosities were biologically molded by Giants in ancient times, created as a ruthless siege weapon to hunt and kill Dragons during millennia-old territorial wars. This genetic origin survives today in the irrational and genetic hatred that the Behir professes against the draconic race.

espantapajaros.habitat: Abandoned Crops, Cursed Farms and Rural Roads
espantapajaros.resistente: Immune to poison and resistant to non-magical physical attacks
espantapajaros.supervivencia: Don't look directly into their eyes if you don't want to be paralyzed with terror. Also, be very careful when encountering one: scarecrows share a dark bond with their master. The moment they enter combat, the witch or wizard who created them is automatically alerted to your presence. Use rapid heat to reduce them to ashes.
espantapajaros.habilidad: It fixes its gaze of necrotic energies or its empty bowls on a victim, temporarily petrifying them with panic. In addition, it attacks by tearing mercilessly with sharp pieces of wood, rusty pitchforks or nails embedded in its hands.
espantapajaros.lore: Endowed with an imitation of life through dark rituals practiced by witches (Hags) or demonologists, scarecrows are not simple mechanical tricks. For them to exist, their creator must magically bind the tormented soul of a slain creature or lesser demon directly to the straw-and-rags doll, giving it life through the power of that spirit. They are posted as watchmen in cursed fields; During the day they remain completely motionless, but at night or in the presence of intruders, they descend from their posts, gaining a deadly agility driven by the rage of the soul imprisoned within them.

xorn.habitat: Elemental Plane of Earth and Deep Caverns
xorn.supervivencia: If you anger them, there is no escape on dry land: they track and 'swim' across solid rock to ambush you from below. If you want to avoid a deadly battle, you can always try to reason with them by offering tributes of gold, gems, or precious metals; They prefer a good banquet to shedding blood.
xorn.habilidad: It can dive through shiny mud, solid stone, and undeformed earth as if they were water, leaving no trail or tunnel behind. His innate seismic sense allows him to perceive the vibrations of any nearby entity or precious stone while he attacks quickly with his three stone arms.
xorn.lore: Originating from the hostile and hyperdense Elemental Plane of Earth, the Despite their terrifying appearance, the Xorn do not devour flesh. They have an insatiable and lethal hunger dictated by the constant consumption of genuine precious metals (gold, platinum) and priceless jewelry. In their extraplanar expeditions towards the Underdark or the dwarf mines, they are capable of sensing fortune in the backpacks of the explorers, laying fierce underground ambushes or demanding their riches as an aggressive and non-negotiable mining "toll."

merrow.habitat: Underwater Coasts, Dark Reefs and Abyssal Caves
merrow.supervivencia: Keep your distance in water combat and avoid being on the edge of boats or docks where they can snag you and drag you to the bottom.
merrow.habilidad: The monstrosity launches a heavy harpoon attached to a rope. If it hits, it can drag the victim up to 20 feet under the dark waters in an instant.
merrow.lore: They were once proud mermen, but their ancestors fell into corruption after worshiping idols of the deep. Transformed by demonic energies, they are now cruel deep-sea hunters who emerge to claim victims and drag them to their submerged lairs, where they perform dark carnivorous rituals.

notico.habitat: Forgotten Dungeons, Magical Ruins and Arcane Archives
notico.supervivencia: Don't let him hold your gaze and mentally hide your fears; It feeds on the secrets and paranoia of those who invade its territory.
notico.habilidad: With its single cyclopean eye, the noticus can cause tissue breakdown (necrotic damage). Furthermore, it penetrates the minds of its victims, pulling out and unearthing dark secrets.
notico.lore: Formerly they were sorcerers obsessed with accumulating forbidden arcane knowledge. As punishment for delving into mysteries too deep—often bequeathed by Vecna—their minds fractured and their bodies warped into these horrendous aberrations. Now they lurk in broken libraries or deep dungeons, always drooling for magical knowledge and dark secrets they can never unravel.

minotauro.supervivencia: Don't try to run in straight hallways, use agility and corners to evade their onslaught; Trying to lose them in a place they consider home is futile.
minotauro.habilidad: This fearsome creature perfectly remembers any path it has traveled and charges with overwhelming fury, impaling intruders with its immense horns before hacking them to pieces with its great axe.
minotauro.lore: Originating from the pure chaos of the Underdark or ancient corrupted druidic rituals, the Minotaurs were born to be the devious guardians of abyssal complexes and labyrinths. Fierce and driven by an uncontrollable rage fueled by the cult of Baphomet, their unnatural orientation is paralleled by the horror that instills their deafening scream before a devastating attack.

otyugh.supervivencia: Don't let them get close; use fire to purge them and stay away from areas of extreme waste or stagnant water, as they attack from below like perfect ambushers.
otyugh.habilidad: It pounces its painful tentacles full of thorns on its prey to immobilize them and bring them closer to its fearsome jaws. A bite from the otyugh transmits serious diseases.
otyugh.lore: Insatiable monsters born of rot, Otyughs are monstrosities with three muscular legs and tentacles ending in patches of spikes, topped by a three-eyed bulbous sensor. Generally ignored by intelligent beings as long as they live to eat garbage, filth, or unfortunate intruders from deep caves or sewers; They use rudimentary telepathy to search for tasty corpses.

mastin_sombrio.habitat: Dreary Places, Night Forests and Graves of Gloom
mastin_sombrio.resistente: Necrotic, Non-Magical Weapons in the Dark
mastin_sombrio.supervivencia: Intense, radiant light is its greatest weakness. Use torches, crossfire, or spells like 'Daylight' to remove their natural camouflage and decrease their lethality.
mastin_sombrio.habilidad: They become virtually invisible in areas of dim light or darkness, and their powerful, icy howl can freeze the blood and instill absolute panic over a wide radius.
mastin_sombrio.lore: Canine beasts originating from the planes of shadows, brought to this magical realm by dark sects or wild magic. These terrifying hunting dogs are the favorite pets and sentinels of dark deities, formidable werewolves or vampires. They measure the size of a stocky pony but lack natural fur, looking like hellhounds entirely composed of dense shadows that do not reflect light.

saga.habitat: Swamps, Twisted Forests and Lonely Moors
saga.supervivencia: Don't trust strangers in desolate places and never make a deal or accept gifts from a Saga; his contract magic always has a twisted trap.
saga.habilidad: Able to imitate any sound and disguise her gruesome figure in the form of a beautiful young maiden or a helpless old woman, she uses magic to trick the unwary before tearing them apart with her sharp, iron-like claws.
saga.lore: Dark sisters of nature, the sagas are macabre fey corrupted by rancor and malevolence. They savor the misery and pain of others, creating intricate networks of deception to ruin lives. Those who form a Coven share an Eye of Saga and gain access to destructive arcane magics. They are masters of potions of dubious origin and prophecies wrapped in curses.

manticora.habitat: High Mountains, Dense Forests and Steep Caverns
manticora.supervivencia: Manticores are extremely proud and cruel. Don't try to flee in a straight line, seek the cover of heavy trees or structures to evade their deadly flying thorns.
manticora.habilidad: With a furious swing of its tail, the manticore can launch volleys of enormous, sharp spear-like spikes at its prey from the air, pinning them to the ground mercilessly.
manticora.lore: A horror crafted by ancient magic, the manticore has the robust body of a wild lion, the imposing leathery wings of a dragon, a deadly thorn-covered tail, and a disturbing, vaguely humanoid face that reflects sadistic intelligence. These beasts love to talk to their victims before tearing them apart, licking their fear and offering false hope of escape just for fun. As undisputed owners of their aerial territories, they rarely tolerate intruders or competition.

leviatan.supervivencia: Never face a Leviathan in the open sea; seeks to escape to dry land, or aerial areas. Its size and speed in the water are lethal.
leviatan.habilidad: Create monstrous waves at will to sweep away your rivals. Furthermore, his immense elemental body generates large magical currents of water over a large area.
leviatan.lore: The Leviathan is the destructive embodiment of the ocean and aquatic storms. Normally isolated in the ocean depths, when it emerges to the surface it causes disasters on the scale of tsunamis. It is a mythical entity, a living calamity of great power.

zaratan.habitat: Mountains, Rocky Deserts and Land Planes
zaratan.resistente: Cold, Fire, Lightning, Bludgeoning, Slashing, and Piercing Damage from Nonmagical Weapons
zaratan.supervivencia: It's like fighting a moving mountain. Attack from great heights or use spells that ignore his formidable physical defenses and focus on his precarious agility.
zaratan.habilidad: His simple walk generates powerful tremors that fracture the earth and collapse buildings. It can retract into its shell becoming nearly indestructible and spit out debris.
zaratan.lore: A Zaratan is an earth elemental of apocalyptic proportions. It is often mistaken for a large hill or mountain that suddenly comes to life and causes tremors in its wake. It symbolizes the immutability and cataclysmic wrath of the earth itself.

kruthik.supervivencia: Try to maintain high ground or position yourself on hardened surfaces where they cannot dig in and ambush you; Also, always watch your rear.
kruthik.habilidad: They take advantage of their numbers by attacking solitary or disoriented targets all at once, also launching thorny spikes from their bodies with great precision.
kruthik.lore: Reptilian, armored monstrosities that combine characteristics of wolves and large insects. Kruthiks create large underground hives. They aggressively devour anything that crosses the galleries near their colony.

driade.habilidad_titulo: Arboreal Translation, Innate Magic and Fey Charm
driade.habilidad: A dryad can merge with the wood of surrounding trees to instantly teleport up to 18 meters to another tree. In addition to his passive magic resistance, he can innately cast 'Strong Skin', 'Entangle', and 'Pass Without a Trace'. His powerful fey voice allows him to Charm (Wisdom DC 14) up to three humanoids or beasts simultaneously; those under its spell will protect the dryad with their own lives until the effect wears off or they take damage.
driade.lore: Dryads are the guardian spirits par excellence of unexplored forests, intrinsically linked to the heartbeat of a single ancient tree to which their soul remains tied; If her tree dies, the dryad will descend into deep madness before perishing irrevocably. They tend to be elusive, peacefully spying on intruders from the dense foliage, only showing themselves when they violate the tranquility of the flora with indiscriminate cruelty. Their priority and punitive defensive method silently focuses on bending the natural will of others, turning aggressors against their own lumberjack allies.

variantes.habitat: Dungeons, Graveyards, Any Place with Permanent Darkness
variantes.supervivencia: NEVER face her in total darkness: each hit that drains your Strength can kill you without reducing you to 0 HP. If your Strength reaches 0, you die and respawn as another Shadow. Keep a radiant light active and eliminate it quickly: in darkness it can become almost invisible.
variantes.habilidad: His touch reduces the target's Strength by 1d4. If Strength reaches 0, the target dies and in 1d4 hours is resurrected as a new Shadow under its control. The Shadow is almost impossible to detect in areas of dim light or darkness.
variantes.lore: Shadows are not creatures of the Plane of Shadows wandering lost. They are what remains of a mortal whose soul was consumed by darkness: neither spirit, nor body, just the hollow silhouette of something that once had a will. They stick to the walls, imitate the shape of the living and wait. And when they attack, they do not hit the flesh, but the very force of living.

variantes.habitat: Tombs, Ruins, Sites of Violent Death
variantes.supervivencia: They are fast and pass through walls: do not use the terrain as a tactical advantage against them. Its drain reduces the maximum HP, not just the current one. Kill the controlling Wraith or Apparition first; Without a teacher they can be disoriented.
variantes.habilidad: His touch deals 3d6 necrotic damage and reduces the target's maximum HP by that amount until the next long rest. Pass through objects and solid walls without penalty. In direct sunlight, you have disadvantage on your attack rolls.
variantes.lore: The specter is the simplest residue of a violent and unresolved death. He has no agenda, he has no intact memories, he does not understand the time that has passed. He only knows that something was taken from him and that the living have what he can no longer have. The most powerful Apparitions can create wraiths by killing humans, turning them into eternal servants of their own misery.

variantes.habitat: Haunted Houses, Places with Hoarded Objects, Sealed Tombs
variantes.supervivencia: It is invisible by default: detecting it requires active perception or magic. Can throw objects in the environment as projectiles. Clear the area of ​​furniture and heavy objects before engaging him: without ammunition, his danger is drastically reduced.
variantes.habilidad: He can move objects up to 150kg with his mind, using them as projectiles (4d10 damage, pushes the target). Remains invisible except when attacking. Shares the disembodiment of the spectrum: passes through solids without penalty.
variantes.lore: Unlike the specter that attacks directly, the poltergeist prefers chaos at a distance. It closes doors, throws furniture, makes beams fall. In its first manifestations it can be confused with a natural phenomenon or a broken mechanism. When the adventurers discover what surrounds them, the poltergeist already knows the layout of each trap that he has prepared with the objects in the environment.

variantes.habitat: Cursed Swamps, Swamps, Flooded Graveyards, Caverns
variantes.resistente: Lightning (Immune), Poison (Immune), almost all physical damage; Incorporeal
variantes.supervivencia: His AC of 19 makes him very difficult to hit with physical weapons. Use force spells or area magic. His tactic is to guide you into dangerous terrain (quicksand, cliffs, traps) while absorbing the vitality of the dying.
variantes.habilidad: When an adjacent creature falls to 0 HP, the Wisp can absorb its life energy, recovering 10d6 HP. Can become invisible as a bonus action. Its light can change color and intensity to imitate torches, stars or distress signals.
variantes.lore: The will-o'-the-wisp is a patient hunter who never runs. It appears as a flickering luminosity in the distance, just enough to look like a torch or an exit. He guides travelers through swamps and swamps until the terrain kills them for him. It then devours their life energy as they sink. In some arcane texts it is suggested that will-o'-the-wisps are the spirits of tricksters or liars, condemned to deceive forever.

variantes.habitat: Places Where He Died, Haunted Buildings, Ruins with History
